title: De quibusdam eximiis proprietatibus circa divisores potestatum occurrentibus

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the paper fixes a number a. The letters T (resp. Θ) denote the residues r ≡ 1 (mod 4) modulo 4a such that every prime 2m+1 ≡ ±r (mod 4a) divides a^m − 1 (resp. a^m + 1). In modern terms, T is the set of classes with (a/p) = +1 and Θ the set with (a/p) = −1. Euler's criterion makes the two descriptions equivalent. Euler's form of quadratic reciprocity guarantees that this depends only on p mod 4a.

The previous page (Problema §30) treats composite a = fg. If f^m ≡ g^m ≡ 1 or f^m ≡ g^m ≡ −1 (mod p), then (fg)^m ≡ 1. This is multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol in its upper entry: (fg/p) = (f/p)(g/p).

This page completes the rule:
- T(fg) = (T(f) ∩ T(g)) ∪ (Θ(f) ∩ Θ(g)), after lifting each list to a full period modulo 4fg.
- Θ(fg) = (T(f) ∩ Θ(g)) ∪ (T(g) ∩ Θ(f)).
- Equivalently, Θ(fg) consists of the remaining 4n+1 residues prime to a.

Example §31, a = 15:
- For 3: T = 1 mod 12 and Θ = 5 mod 12, lifted mod 60.
- For 5: T = {1, 9} mod 20 (p ≡ ±1 mod 5) and Θ = {13, 17} mod 20.
- Intersections give T(15) = {1, 17, 49, 53} and Θ(15) = {13, 29, 37, 41} mod 60. 25 and 65 are dropped as not prime to 15.
- Euler observes that all 4n+1 residues prime to 15 appear, split equally between T and Θ.

Scholion §32 explains the count with the totient product formula. φ(N) = ∏ (p−1)p^(α−1), so φ(60) = 16. Half of these (8) are ≡ 1 mod 4, and half of those (4) go to T and 4 to Θ. The next pages tabulate a = 6, 10, 14, 22, 26, 15, 21.

In modern language: n ↦ (a/n), the Jacobi/Kronecker symbol, is a quadratic character mod 4a. It is nontrivial on the 1-mod-4 subgroup when a is not a square, so its kernel has index 2.
errors: No computational errors on this page: T(3), Θ(3), T(5), Θ(5), the intersections and the final lists for 15 all check (e.g. (15/17) = (3/17)(5/17) = (−1)(−1) = 1; (15/13) = (3/13)(5/13) = 1·(−1) = −1).

Gap: 'totidem semper terminos in vtrumque ordinem T et Θ ingredi' is asserted from inspection, without proof. It is false when a is a square (Θ empty), which Euler himself notes on the next page (§33). The correct reason (T is a subgroup of index 2 of the 4n+1 residues prime to 4a when a is not a square) is not given.

ideas.what: Combining residue/non-residue classes for a = fg: T = (T_f∩T_g)∪(Θ_f∩Θ_g), Θ = (T_f∩Θ_g)∪(Θ_f∩T_g)
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol (fg/p) = (f/p)(g/p); quadratic character mod 4a as a product of characters
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Euler's criterion and Euler's work; formalized by Legendre (1798) and Gauss (1801)
ideas.where_published: E557 itself (Opuscula analytica I, 1783); related material in E552 and earlier quadratic-residue papers (E164, E449)

ideas.what: Prime divisors of a^m ∓ 1 (p = 2m+1) are determined by p mod 4a
ideas.modern_name: Euler's formulation of quadratic reciprocity / Euler's criterion

ideas.what: Number of integers below N coprime to N equals ∏(p−1)p^(α−1)
Observation that T and Θ contain equally many classes (for non-square a)
ideas.modern_name: Kernel of a nontrivial quadratic character has index 2; equidistribution of residues/non-residues among classes

deep.surprise_reason: Standard content of a well-known published paper (Opera Omnia I.4) on Euler's form of quadratic reciprocity. The multiplicative combination rule and the totient formula are Euler's known results; the equal-split observation is a simple character fact.
transcription_corrections: Line 'vt eo referantur termini litteris T^(f) et Θ^(g), quam litteris T^(g) et Θ^(f) communes': the image appears to read 'vt eo referantur tam termini litteris T(f) et Θ(g), quam litteris T(g) et Θ(f) communes' (the 'tam' is missing).
